one_month_reasoning: ALAB's own Q3 2026 report is expected Nov 2-5, 2026 (not yet announced), i.e. just after the Oct 29 window, so the main company-specific catalyst falls outside it. Inside the window: hyperscaler Q3 earnings and 2027 capex commentary (Alphabet/Microsoft/Meta around Oct 27-29; Amazon possibly Oct 29-30, on the edge), which matter directly because AWS Trainium3 is the Scorpio X anchor. Sell-side and BofA/Goldman see 2027 hyperscaler capex at ~$1.1-1.2T and nobody cut spending after the Sept 14 AI-slowdown selloff, so I lean mildly positive on capex prints, but the stock already rebounded from ~$289 (Sept 8) to ~$358 and remains headline-sensitive. Net: essentially symmetric lognormal around ~$356 with sigma 0.27 (annual realized vol 99% / 3.5 = 0.28), no directional call.

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (CY2028E EPS ~$8.3 x 40x = $332, weight 0.6) and forward EV/sales (CY2028E revenue ~$3.86B x 15x + ~$1.5B net cash over ~190M diluted shares = $313, weight 0.4), giving ~$324 fair value at Sept 2027.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: CY2028E non-GAAP EPS $8.3 (2027 consensus $6.39 x 1.30) x 40x forward multiple, applied at Sept 2027 when the market will price 2028

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus 2027 growth is ~56-59%; halved-ish deceleration to 30% for 2028, consistent with Marvell guiding data center >60% in FY28, Broadcom guiding AI revenue doubling in FY28, and Goldman/BofA 2027 hyperscaler capex ~+35-50%, but haircut for AWS's planned shift of Trainium4 to NVLink Fusion ending PCIe-based Scorpio X scale-up revenue.

Stock currently trades ~56x 2027 consensus EPS ($357.84/$6.39); high-growth AI connectivity peers (Credo, Broadcom) trade at lower multiples as growth normalizes; 40x on a year-forward EPS at a point when growth decelerates toward ~30% is a de-rating from today's multiple.

methods.name: EV/sales
methods.inputs: CY2028E revenue $3.86B (2027 consensus $2.97B x 1.30) x 15x EV/sales + ~$1.5B net cash, / ~190M diluted shares

inputs_detail.derivation: 2027 consensus x 1.30, same growth logic as P/E method

~72-74% gross margin and ~39% non-GAAP operating margin (Q2 2026) support a premium semis multiple; current EV/2027 sales is ~(66.2B-1.25B)/2.97B = ~22x; assume de-rating to 15x on 2028 as growth slows.
Cash + marketable securities $1.25B at June 30 2026, no debt; plus a year of FCF partly offset by buybacks/withholding -> ~$1.5B.
Q3 2026 guidance of ~185M weighted diluted shares plus ~2-3% annual dilution from SBC.

bear.story: AI capex digestion (post Sept-2026 slowdown rhetoric turns into actual 2027-28 budget cuts) or Scorpio X/Trainium3 ramp disappoints; Broadcom Tomahawk Ultra/Ethernet scale-up and Marvell (XConn, Structera) take share; AWS's Trainium4 NVLink Fusion move pulls forward the end of PCIe scale-up. 2028 EPS ~$6.5 at ~28x.

base.story: Q3 lands near $550M guide, Scorpio becomes the largest line, 2027 revenue ~$3B with beats; P-Series wins at 3 hyperscalers + 2 new ones and UALink/optical ramp partially offset Scorpio X maturity; multiple de-rates from ~56x to ~42x on higher 2028 EPS.

bull.story: Hyperscaler capex reaches Goldman's $1.2T+ in 2027, Amazon's $6.5B warrant-backed purchase commitment front-loads, UALink and optical engines win additional XPU programs, 2028 EPS >$11 and market keeps a ~55x multiple.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$200 (-44%, about 31x my 2028E EPS or ~31x 2027 consensus) the price would imply the market no longer believes in ~$3B 2027 revenue: most likely a Scorpio X/Trainium3 ramp problem, a hyperscaler share loss to Broadcom/Marvell/NVLink Fusion, or genuine AI capex cuts rather than ordinary 99%-vol swings (the stock traded ~$98 to ~$499 in the last year).

catalysts.event: Hyperscaler Q3 earnings and 2027 capex commentary (Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta, Amazon)
ALAB Q3 2026 results vs $540-560M guide; Q4 guide and Scorpio X ramp
AWS re:Invent: Trainium3 deployment scale, Trainium4/NVLink Fusion timing
Broadcom FQ4 results: scale-up Ethernet (Tomahawk Ultra) traction vs PCIe/UALink
NVIDIA GTC: NVLink Fusion adoption by custom XPU vendors
First UALink switch silicon (ALAB, Upscale AI, Marvell) and hyperscaler adoption decisions

key_uncertainties: Durability of 2027-28 hyperscaler AI capex after the Sept 2026 AI-slowdown statements (no cuts so far)
Length of the Scorpio X revenue window before AWS moves Trainium4 to NVLink Fusion
Whether open scale-up standardizes on UALink (favors ALAB) or Ethernet/ESUN via Broadcom Tomahawk Ultra
Competitive pressure on Aries retimers and P-Series switches from Broadcom and Marvell (XConn acquisition)
Customer concentration and multiple compression from ~56x 2027 EPS
reasoning: Company facts: Q2 2026 revenue $392M (+104% y/y), non-GAAP EPS $0.80, Q3 guide $540-560M (+40% q/q) and non-GAAP EPS $1.16-1.21, ~$1.25B cash, no debt. Industry chain is strongly supportive near term: Broadcom FQ3 AI revenue +221% with FY27/FY28 AI revenue guided to double each year; Marvell raised FY28 revenue to $18B with data center >60% growth; Credo FQ1 +115% y/y guiding >85% FY growth; Goldman/BofA see 2027 hyperscaler capex $1.08-1.2T, and no hyperscaler cut spending after the Sept 14 Amodei/Altman/Musk slowdown calls that knocked ALAB -10%. But the same chain signals competition converging on ALAB's growth engine: Broadcom's Tomahawk Ultra seeing 'surprising' scale-up adoption, Marvell buying XConn (PCIe/CXL switches) and partnering with NVIDIA on NVLink Fusion, and newsletter analysis that AWS Trainium4 moves to NVLink Fusion, bounding Scorpio X's life. Valuation: today's $357.84 is ~56x 2027 consensus EPS $6.39; applying a de-rated 40x to my 2028E $8.3 plus an EV/sales cross-check gives ~$324 fair value a year out, slightly below spot, while the company's beat-and-raise pattern argues for a base case near $370. Scenarios $190/$370/$620 at 25/50/25. With 99% realized vol I use a lognormal-like distribution with median ~$355 and sigma ~0.68 (below realized vol because realized includes the post-2025 re-rating; still far above a typical large cap's 25-35%), slightly fattened in the lower-middle for capex-cycle risk. Research limited to ~13 queries/fetches; sell-side estimates from an aggregator.
